title.description: Use a clear business-intelligence title. Do not use hype.

introduction.description: Start with 1-2 calm framing paragraphs before key takeaways.
required_pattern: Start with the ZNBW assessment, not the statistic.
Explain the business signal in plain language.
Mention the strongest verified data point only after the interpretation is clear.
avoid: Generic phrases such as 'continued to rise'
Overexplaining before the reader knows why it matters

key_takeaways.format: Each key takeaway must link to a later article section using markdown anchor links.
key_takeaways.style: Strategic, business-facing, concise. Each takeaway should be decision-useful, not merely descriptive.

content_sections.description: Use clear analytical sections. Explain what happened, what the data shows, and the underlying mechanism.

znbw_assessment.placement: After Key Takeaways or as the first content section.
znbw_assessment.purpose: State the central interpretation of the article in one short paragraph.

why_it_matters_to_business.description: Explain practical relevance for operators, investors, planners, and decision makers. This section should translate the data into commercial or strategic relevance.

graph_rules.placement: Inside relevant article sections, not grouped at the end.
rules: Every graph placeholder must support a nearby paragraph.
Prefer indexed comparisons when comparing sectors.
Use multi-series graphs where the supplied graph packages support comparison.
Forecast placeholders may only be used when forecast data exists or when clearly labelled as a future requirement.
Executive diagrams, country maps, and institutional explainers are allowed only when they directly support the article.

transparency_panel.description: Include confidence, evidence base, data coverage, primary mechanism, limitations, and source notes.

sources.description: List source names, tables, rows, dates, and URLs where available. Keep sources factual and directly traceable to the supplied package.

tone: Calm, factual, structured, business-oriented, institutional. Avoid hype.
